results.title: Design and Quality for Biomedical Technologies XIX
results.content: We have developed a non-clinical bench test method using a mock cardiovascular flow loop and tissue-mimicking finger phantom that can simulate bio-realistic pulsation at controlled blood oxygen saturation (SaO2) levels. Design of a microfluidic blood flow phantom to address skin tone bias in multispectral imaging for nailfold capillaroscopy. Standardized tissue-mimicking phantoms for quantitative photoacoustic imaging (Invited Paper). SFDI is finding utility in a wide array of applications, including burn assessment, skin cancer detection, tumor monitoring, brain imaging, vascularization studies, and evaluating food quality—thanks to its non-invasive, wide-field, and depth-sensitive optical property mapping capabilities. Design of Lipid Emulsion-Dye Phantoms for Validation of Optical Imaging Systems. The homemade lipid emulsion-dye phantom has a low cost and tunability and can provide a more accessible approach to validating various optical imaging systems. Gelatin-based tissue-simulating skin phantom for the optimization of enhanced thermal imaging (ETI). The development of tissue-simulating phantoms to validate the quality and precision of medical imaging systems is a well-established field.

results.content: In addition to any other authority specified in these procedures, the reviewing official and the presiding official, with respect to those authorities involving the oral presentation, shall have the authority to issue orders; examine witnesses; take all steps necessary for the conduct of an orderly hearing; rule on requests and motions; grant extensions of time for good reasons; dismiss for failure to meet deadlines or other requirements; order the parties to submit relevant information or witnesses; remand a case for further action by the respondent; waive or modify these procedures in a specific case, usually with notice to the parties; reconsider a decision of the reviewing official where a party promptly alleges a clear error of fact or law; and to take any other action necessary to resolve disputes in accordance with the objectives of these procedures. Before any legal action is filed in court challenging the suspension or proposed revocation, respondent shall exhaust administrative remedies provided under this subpart, unless otherwise provided by Federal Law. The reviewing official's decision, under Section 16.9(e) or 16.14(a) constitutes final agency action and is ripe for judicial review as of the date of the decision.

results.content: See *Data.CMS.gov,* Medicare Shared Savings Program, Accountable Care Organizations, Public Use File (by performance year, for PY 2025), available at *https://data.cms.gov/​medicare-shared-savings-program/​accountable-care-organizations.*. Message to the Quality Payment Program listserv on January 4, 2025, entitled “The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) is Soliciting Stakeholder Recommendations for Potential Consideration of New Specialty Measure Sets and/or Revisions to the Existing Specialty Measure Sets for the 2026 Performance Year of the Merit-based Incentive Payment System (MIPS).”. Section 101(b) of the Medicare Access and CHIP Reauthorization Act of 2015 (MACRA) sunset the Medicare EHR Incentive Program for Eligible Professionals, set forth at section 1848(o) of the Act. As discussed previously, section 1848(o)(2) of the Act has been incorporated into the MIPS Promoting Interoperability performance category's requirements via section 1848(q)(2)(B)(iv) of the Act. See CY 2017 Quality Payment Program final rule (81 FR 77018 and 77019) for more information regarding the sunsetting of the Medicare EHR Incentive Program for Eligible Professionals.
